requirements.text: For vehicles with a lower bumper height of less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.1.

For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the bumper shall meet either the requirements of paragraph 4.1.1 (lower legform) or 4.1.2 (upper legform), at the choice of the manufacturer.
For vehicles with a lower bumper height greater than or equal to 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 4.1.2.

Where the lower legform to bumper test applies, compliance with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.1 shall be verified using the flexible lower legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.1.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, compliance with the performance requirements of paragraph 5.1.2 shall be verified using the upper legform impactor specified in paragraph 6.3.1.2 and the test procedures specified in paragraph 7.1.2.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1 (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament (MCL) elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1 (flexible lower legform to bumper), the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.

When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.1 (flexible lower legform to bumper), the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm; however, the manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm (a Contracting Party may restrict application of this relaxation zone).
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2 (upper legform to bumper), the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
When tested in accordance with paragraph 7.1.2 (upper legform to bumper), the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
Where the vehicle is tested as a DPPS (deployable pedestrian protection system triggered by the pedestrian impact sensors), the headform test conditions and requirements in Annex 1 shall apply.

Where parts of the bumper module (e.g. upper grille/fascia) lie within the child headform test area, when tested with the child headform in accordance with paragraphs 7.2, 7.3 and, if applicable, Annex 1, the HIC shall comply with paragraph 5.2.3.

Where headform tests apply to the front structure, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area and 1,000 over two thirds of the combined child and adult headform test areas, and the HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
In case there is only a child headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area and shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining area.
At the time of testing, the vehicle or sub-system shall have a relative humidity of 40 % ± 30 % and a stabilized temperature of 20 ± 4 °C.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body, adjusted to the conditions of paragraph 6.2.1, shall be used for the test.
The vehicle shall be tested in its normal ride attitude, either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

In case a cut-body is used, it shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure (including the complete bumper module), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user, to demonstrate the performance and interactions of all contributory vehicle components.
In case a cut-body is used, it shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

All devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle (e.g. a deployable system triggered by the pedestrian impact sensors) shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.
The manufacturer shall show that any device designed to protect vulnerable road users will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

Where vehicle components (other than active pedestrian protection devices) could change shape or position and have more than one fixed shape or position (e.g. an openable charging flap or cover), the vehicle shall comply with the components in each fixed shape or position.
When tested as a DPPS, the vehicle shall be adjusted as specified in the test procedure defined in Annex 1.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the selected target points shall be in the bumper test area.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the direction of the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ± 2° at the time of first contact, and the impactor axis perpendicular to the horizontal plane with a roll and pitch tolerance of ± 2°.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the bottom of the impactor shall be 75 ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the selected target points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 3.10.

In the upper legform to bumper test, the direction of impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle with the axis of the upper legform vertical at the time of first contact, with a tolerance of ± 2°.

In the upper legform to bumper test, at the time of first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line with a ± 10 mm tolerance, and positioned laterally at the selected impact location with a tolerance of ± 10 mm.
In the upper legform to bumper test, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 ± 0.2 m/s.
Where child headform tests apply, they shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 3.13.

Where child headform tests apply, selected impact points shall be, at the time of first contact, a minimum of 82.5 mm inside the side reference lines, forward of the WAD1700 line or a minimum of 82.5 mm forward of the bonnet rear reference line (whichever is most forward), and rearward of the WAD1000 line or a minimum of 82.5 mm rearward of the bonnet leading edge reference line (whichever is most rearward).
Where child headform tests apply, the headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 ± 0.2 m/s.
Where child headform tests apply, the direction of impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, downward and rearward, at an angle of 50 ± 2° to the horizontal.

For a vehicle fitted with a Deployable Pedestrian Protection System (DPPS) triggered by the pedestrian impact sensors, the vehicle manufacturer shall specify the lowest speed of activation (lower deployment velocity threshold) of the DPPS.

For the DPPS system deployment verification, sensor activation tests with the FlexPLI, as specified in paragraph 6.3.1.1 of the Regulation, shall be performed within the detection test area at the DPPS lower deployment velocity threshold, and the DPPS sensing system shall activate the system in these tests.

For the DPPS sensing system verification, a test with the FlexPLI shall be performed at nominal velocity (11.1 m/s) at the vehicle centreline (Y0), and the DPPS sensing system shall activate the system in this test.

If the DPPS is not activated during any of the sensing system verification tests, all headform tests shall be conducted with the DPPS in the undeployed position according to paragraphs 7.2 to 7.4 of the Regulation.

For DPPS sensing system verification tests with a stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition as specified by the manufacturer for a vehicle speed corresponding to the particular use case.
The DPPS Total Response Time (TRT) shall be confirmed by using the FlexPLI at a vehicle speed of 11.1 m/s and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).
The DPPS Sensing Time (ST) shall be measured either independently or during a TRT measurement test, at the vehicle speed specified in the Regulation and at the vehicle centreline (Y0).

If the measured DPPS Sensing Time (ST) is within a tolerance of -5 ms/+3 ms of the value specified by the manufacturer, the manufacturer's value shall be used; otherwise, the measured value shall be used for the test.
For dynamic DPPS testing, only the Sensing Time (ST) shall be verified.
For ST/TRT verification tests with a stationary vehicle, the vehicle shall be set to the normal running condition as specified by the manufacturer.
For DPPS sensing and TRT/ST verification tests with the FlexPLI where the moving vehicle impacts the stationary impactor, the tolerances shall be: target speed ±0.6 m/s and impact accuracy ±50 mm.

For DPPS sensing and TRT/ST verification tests with the FlexPLI where a propulsion system propels the impactor against the stationary vehicle, the target speed, impact accuracy and angle tolerances shall be those of the performance tests in paragraph 7.1 of the Regulation.
The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark.
The ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the type designation.

ESAs brought to the market as replacement parts do not need a type approval if they are obviously marked as a replacement part by an identification number and if they are identical and from the same manufacturer as the corresponding original equipment.

In case an ESA is (part of) a light source (e.g. the LED side signalling lamp or decorative lighting module), the applicant shall either specify the approval number granted to this ESA according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128, or provide a test report by a designated Technical Service stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; without this documentation, R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted (para. 4.2.4).

ESAs which are intentional RF transmitters (e.g. radar sensor, active keyless-entry aerial) and which have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.
The ESA approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The ESA approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle.
Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
The ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

ESA broadband radiated emission limit (Annex 7 method): 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6).
ESA broadband radiated emission limit (Annex 7 method): constant 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

ESA narrowband radiated emission limit (Annex 8 method): 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7).
ESA narrowband radiated emission limit (Annex 8 method): constant 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
Where an ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8 (narrowband emissions).
The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 1.
Maximum allowed positive transient pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on supply lines: +75 V for 12 V systems, +150 V for 24 V systems.
Maximum allowed negative transient pulse amplitude emitted by the ESA on supply lines: -100 V for 12 V systems, -450 V for 24 V systems.

ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9 (stripline, TEM cell, BCI, ALSE/absorber chamber, reverberation chamber).

ESA radiated immunity test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2a), per chosen method: Stripline 60 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).

ESA radiated immunity minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band (Table 2b), per chosen method: Stripline 50 V/m (20-400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20-200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20-400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80-2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF-2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000-6,000 MHz).
During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the ESA's "immunity related functions".
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and Annex 9.

For ESAs containing receivers, loss of function of the receiver during the immunity test, when the test signal is within the receiver bandwidth (RF exclusion band) as specified for the radio service/product in the harmonized international EMC standard, does not necessarily lead to fail criteria.
ESAs that are RF transmitters (e.g. radar sensor, active keyless-entry aerial) shall be tested in the transmit mode.
For RF transmitting ESAs, wanted emissions within the necessary bandwidth and out-of-band emissions are disregarded for the purpose of this Regulation.
For RF transmitting ESAs, spurious emissions (harmonic, parasitic, intermodulation and frequency conversion products) are subject to the emission requirements of this Regulation.

The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The starting profile shall be assessed according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1, and the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor: starting profile immunity at level II (12 V and 24 V systems), 10 pulses; functional status B for ESAs related to immunity related functions which shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESAs related to immunity related functions, and D for ESAs not related to immunity related functions.
Test pulse 1 immunity: -75 V (12 V system) / -450 V (24 V system), 500 pulses; FPSC III for ESAs related and not related to immunity related functions.
Test pulse 2a immunity: +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems), 500 pulses; FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions, III for ESAs not related.
Test pulse 2b immunity: +10 V (12 V system) / +20 V (24 V system), 10 pulses; FPSC II for ESAs related to immunity related functions, III for ESAs not related.
Test pulse 3a immunity: -112 V (12 V system) / -150 V (24 V system), 1 h; FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions, III for ESAs not related.
Test pulse 3b immunity: +75 V (12 V system) / +150 V (24 V system), 1 h; FPSC I for ESAs related to immunity related functions, III for ESAs not related.

Each ESA of the bumper module (camera, radar, radar/LIDAR with heating, PDC sensor, pedestrian impact sensors, temperature sensor, decorative and signalling lighting, keyless-entry aerial, wiring harness) approved under this Regulation shall be manufactured to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.

For conformity of production of an ESA taken from the series, the measured broadband and narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed the reference limits prescribed in paragraphs 6.5.2.1 and 6.6.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).

For conformity of production of an ESA taken from the series, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength (V/m) up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.

For conformity of production of a component or STU (ESA) taken from the series, the component shall show no degradation of performance of 'immunity related functions' up to the conducted disturbance levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
For conformity of production of a component or STU (ESA) taken from the series, the conducted transient emission of the component shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (reference limits referred to in paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E (dBµV/m) = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) in the 30-75 MHz band and E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) in the 75-400 MHz band, F being the frequency in MHz.

The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (reference limits referred to in paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1.), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 63 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz band.

The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (reference limits referred to in paragraph 6.6.2.1.), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E (dBµV/m) = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) in the 30-75 MHz band and E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) in the 75-400 MHz band, F being the frequency in MHz.

The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA (reference limits referred to in paragraph 6.6.2.1.), measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 53 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz band.
The approval mark affixed to an ESA (Model A, or Model B where combined with other UN Regulation approvals) shall have the characteristic dimension a of at least 6 mm.

The broadband electromagnetic emission test of each ESA of the bumper module (camera, radar, radar/LIDAR incl. heating, PDC, pedestrian impact sensors, temperature sensor, decorative and signalling lighting, keyless-entry aerial, wiring harness) shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
During the broadband emission test according to Annex 7, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), the ESA broadband emission test may be performed on an open area test site (OATS) complying with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.
The ESA broadband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.

ESA broadband emission measurements may be performed with either quasi-peak or peak detectors; the limits of paragraph 6.5 are for quasi-peak detectors, and if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
The narrowband electromagnetic emission test of each ESA of the bumper module shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
During the narrowband emission test according to Annex 8, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4 of CISPR 25.
As an alternative to an ALSE, the ESA narrowband emission test may be performed on an open area test site (OATS) complying with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.
The ESA narrowband emission limits apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
ESA narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.

For immunity to electromagnetic radiation, each ESA of the bumper module may comply with any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion, provided the full frequency range of Annex 9 paragraph 3.1 is covered: absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline (ISO 11452-5), reverberation chamber (ISO 11452-11); frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA immunity test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.

During the immunity test the ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, and arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the ESA immunity test signal shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, unless otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

Where the absorber chamber test is used for ESA immunity, the 'substitution method' shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2 and the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
Where TEM cell testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.

Where bulk current injection testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench either with substitution method and injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA, or with closed loop method and injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA; alternatively the ESA may be tested installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with substitution method and injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA.
Where stripline testing is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
Where the reverberation chamber test is used for ESA immunity, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11 using, unless otherwise specified, a test setup with ground plane.
The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESAs (12/24 V) shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (without 12 V/24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

Where the bumper module (e.g. the grille) is fitted with a badge, mascot or other structure that would bend back or retract under an applied load of maximum 100 N, this load shall be applied before and/or while the measurements (reference lines, bumper heights, test areas) are taken.
Where the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.1.

Where the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the bumper shall meet either the flexible lower legform requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. or the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
Where the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2.

Flexible lower legform to bumper: when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.

Flexible lower legform to bumper: when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.

Flexible lower legform to bumper: when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1, the absolute value of dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm; however, the manufacturer may nominate bumper test widths up to a maximum of 264 mm in total where the absolute value of the tibia bending moment shall not exceed 380 Nm (relaxation zone, which a Contracting Party may restrict in its domestic legislation).
Upper legform to bumper: when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
Upper legform to bumper: when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2, the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.

Where parts of the bumper module (e.g. bumper top edge, grille, decorative lighting surround) lie within the bonnet top test area, when tested with the child and adult headforms in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and windscreen test area, and shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the bonnet top test area.

Where parts of the bumper module lie within the headform test area, the HIC for the remaining test areas (outside the two-thirds HIC 1,000 area) shall not exceed 1,700 for both child and adult headforms when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3, 4 and 5.

In case there is only a child headform test area and parts of the bumper module lie within it, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area and shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining area.

Where parts of the bumper module lie within the child headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3 and 4, the child headform HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area and shall not exceed 1,700 for the remaining areas.

A vehicle approved pursuant to UN R127 (including its front bumper module) shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5 (Specifications) of the Regulation.

At the time of pedestrian protection testing, the vehicle or sub-system (including the front bumper module) shall have a relative humidity of 40 per cent ± 30 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C.
Either a complete vehicle or a cut-body shall be used for the pedestrian protection tests of the front bumper module, adjusted to the conditions of Annex 3, paragraphs 3.1.1 and 3.1.2.

Where a complete vehicle is used, the vehicle carrying the bumper module shall be in its normal ride attitude during the test, either securely mounted on raised supports or at rest on a flat horizontal surface with the parking brake applied.

Where a cut-body is used, the cut-body shall include in the test all parts of the vehicle front structure (including the complete bumper module with fascia, absorber, beam, lower stiffener and all attachments), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user.
Where a cut-body is used, the cut-body shall be securely mounted in the normal vehicle ride attitude.

Where a deployable pedestrian protection system triggered by the bumper pedestrian impact sensors is fitted, all devices designed to protect vulnerable road users when impacted by the vehicle shall be correctly activated before and/or be active during the relevant test.

Where a deployable pedestrian protection system is fitted, the manufacturer shall show that the devices (including the pedestrian impact sensors in the bumper) will act as intended in a pedestrian impact.

Where a component of the bumper module, other than an active device to protect pedestrians, could change shape or position and has more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the requirements with the component in each fixed shape or position.
For the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the selected measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

A minimum of three flexible lower legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.

Flexible lower legform to bumper tests shall be made to different types of bumper structure, where they vary throughout the area to be assessed, with selected test points a minimum of 84 mm apart measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the direction of the impact velocity vector shall be in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±2° at the time of first contact.

In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the bottom of the impactor (without parts needed for launching and/or protection) shall be at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact with the bumper.
In the flexible lower legform to bumper test, the impact velocity of the impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies (lower bumper reference line of 500 mm or higher, or at the manufacturer's choice between 425 mm and 500 mm), the selected measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14 of the Regulation.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, a minimum of three upper legform to bumper tests shall be carried out, one each to the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at positions judged to be the most likely to cause injury.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, tests shall be made to different types of bumper structure, where they vary throughout the area to be assessed, with selected measuring points a minimum of 84 mm apart measured horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, the direction of impact shall be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle with the axis of the upper legform vertical at the time of first contact, with a tolerance of ±2°.

Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, at the time of first contact the impactor centre line shall be vertically midway between the upper bumper reference line and the lower bumper reference line (±10 mm) and positioned laterally at the selected impact location (±10 mm).
Where the upper legform to bumper test applies, the impact velocity of the upper legform impactor when striking the bumper shall be 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

Where the bumper top edge, grille or decorative lighting surround lies within the child headform test area, child headform tests shall be made to the front structure within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.16 of the Regulation.
Where parts of the bumper module lie within the child headform test area, the child headform velocity at the time of impact shall be 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.

Where parts of the bumper module lie within the child headform test area, the direction of child headform impact shall be in the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle at an angle of 50° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward for tests to the front structure.

Where the side signalling lamp is part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (e.g. side marker lamp with direction indicator), approval may be granted only if each of these lamps satisfies the provisions of this Regulation or of another Regulation; lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of such a unit.
The lamp shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for 'a' shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light-signalling lamp function(s) for which approval has been granted, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.

The function identification symbols for the side signalling lamp shall be per Table 1: side marker lamp for all vehicle categories 'SM1'; side marker lamp for M1 vehicles 'SM2'; side direction indicator lamp '5' or '6'; front direction indicator lamp '1', '1a', '1b' (or 11, 11a, 11b, 11c), as applicable to the function(s) approved.
The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation (148) followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
If the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.

In the case of a direction indicator of category 1, 1a, 1b (or 11, 11a, 11b, 11c) that cannot be mounted on either side indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
In the case of a direction indicator of category 5 or 6, the horizontal arrow shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle.
For a direction indicator of category 6, an indication 'R' or 'L' shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle.
If the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter 'D' shall be marked to the right side of the function symbol.
If the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter 'Y' shall be marked to the right side of the function symbol.
If the lamp has a reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), it shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case the lamp has replaceable light source(s) (not required for lamps with non-replaceable light sources), the lamp shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
Where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the lamp shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).

In the case of a lamp with non-replaceable light sources, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control and/or a secondary operating mode, the lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module shall bear its specific identification code, comprising the starting letters 'MD' followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1.; the approval mark need not be the same as the one on the lamp, but both marks shall be from the same applicant.
In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the module specific identification code shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a)(ii).
In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with its identification number.
An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of the lamp is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
In case replaceable light source modules are used, the markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a) shall be affixed on the light source module (component).
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3. (a), 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. and 3.3.3.6. do not need to be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle (paragraph 3.3.4.2. does not apply to them).

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the lamps, provided that it is visible after installation and no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.

In case a single approval mark is used for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' (and the Annexes referenced in those sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for lamp type approval, shall apply to the lamp. The requirements pertinent to the lamp and to the vehicle category M1 shall be applied where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 148.
In case the lamp provides a direction indicator function, an assembly of two independent lamps may be type approved as a lamp marked 'D'.
In case the lamp provides a direction indicator function, an interdependent lamp system may be type approved as lamps marked 'Y'.

On request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of the lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components, provided that all requirements for the specific function of UN Regulation No. 148 are fulfilled and the conditions of paragraph 4.5.5. (a) to (d) are met.

Where a logo is incorporated in the lamp, irrespective of the marking requirements of paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer is allowed, and this shall be confirmed by the applicant by a statement (paragraph 3.1.2.2. (f)).

Where a logo is incorporated in the lamp, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.

Where a logo is incorporated in the lamp, notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, the logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) does not have to be symmetrical by itself.
A direction indicator lamp shall not incorporate a logo (in case the side lamp provides a direction indicator function, no logo is permitted in that function).

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source (e.g. side marker lamp or category 5/6 side direction indicator), at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities are not exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in the relevant paragraphs 6.x.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure (noted in the communication form).

In case the lamp is a front direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a or 1b containing more than one light source, instead of paragraph 4.6.1.2. and in addition to paragraph 4.6.1.1., a signal for activation of the tell-tale prescribed in paragraph 6.5.8. of UN Regulation No. 48 shall be produced on the basis of either: (a) any one light source has failed; (b) in the case of a lamp designed for only two light sources, the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum intensity required; or (c) as a consequence of a failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in one of the directions H=0°, V=0°; H=20° outwards, V=+5°; H=10° inwards, V=0° (paragraph 2.1. of Annex 3) is less than the minimum intensity required.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval), and/or light source module(s), and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the prescribed light source category.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) where a category of LED substitute light source is also prescribed, the light source holder shall additionally conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source.
The light-signalling device shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module shall be such that it can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), regardless of the use of tool(s), the light source module shall not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
In the case of replaceable UN approved light sources, all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.

In the case of replaceable UN approved light source(s) controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) used for measurement shall have a luminous flux not deviating more than 5 per cent from the reference/objective luminous flux when test voltage is applied.

In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

In case of a lamp (function) using light sources subject to more than one of the conditions of paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements shall be made separately in accordance with each applicable condition and all separate results shall be added together.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the photometric measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.

Where the lamp, at the discretion of the applicant, also has to be approved with LED substitute light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the prescribed LED substitute light source(s).
If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.

In case measurement results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.

The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling lamp shall be determined; however, in the case of a category 5 or 6 direction indicator, the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems).

In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant (the test laboratory may require the control gear or variable intensity control to be supplied).

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and equipped with replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux, or alternatively at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction of the measured luminous intensities.

In case of a lamp equipped with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources, the lamp shall be operated at a voltage or current setting such that the actual luminous fluxes of the light sources do not deviate by more than 5 per cent from their average luminous flux, with the measured intensities corrected proportionally for the difference between average and reference/objective luminous flux; alternatively, it may be tested using one light source in each individual holder position operating at the reference/objective luminous flux and summing the measured intensities for each direction.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples outside the reference axis shall be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction, or not less than the intensity value specified in that light distribution figure for each direction.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of luminous intensity shall be observed.

When an assembly of two independent lamps of the same function, to be type approved as lamps marked 'D', is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirements when all lamps together are lit.

When an assembly of two independent lamps of the same function, to be type approved as lamps marked 'D', is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the minimum intensity requirements if either lamp has failed.
In case of an interdependent lamp system (marked 'Y'), the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, applying the test procedure of paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions of paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.
Side marker lamps (SM1, SM2): the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 9.

Side marker lamp of category SM1: minimum luminous intensity in the axis of reference 4.0 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(a)); minimum luminous intensity within the standard light distribution 6∙10^-1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(c)); maximum luminous intensity 2.50∙10^1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(b)); standard light distribution per Figure A3-VII; angles of geometric visibility as defined in Table A2-3 with a minimum luminous intensity of 6∙10^-1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(d)).

Side marker lamp of category SM2: minimum luminous intensity in the axis of reference 6∙10^-1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(a)); minimum luminous intensity within the standard light distribution 6∙10^-1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(c)); maximum luminous intensity 2.50∙10^1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(b)); standard light distribution per Figure A3-VIII; angles of geometric visibility as defined in Table A2-3 with a minimum luminous intensity of 6∙10^-1 cd (par. 4.8.3.1.(d)).

Side marker lamps: the colour of the light emitted shall be amber; however, it can be red only if the rearmost side marker lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position lamp, rear end-outline marker lamp, rear fog lamp or stop lamp, or is grouped with or has part of the light emitting surface in common with the rear retroreflector.

Direction indicator lamps of categories 5 and 6: the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 8, with the minimum luminous intensities fulfilled in direction A according to Annex 2.

Direction indicator of category 1: minimum luminous intensity 1.75∙10^2 cd; maximum luminous intensity 1.20∙10^3 cd as a single lamp or 6.00∙10^2 cd as a lamp marked "D"; standard light distribution per Figure A3-I; angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum luminous intensity 3∙10^-1 cd.

Direction indicator of category 1a: minimum luminous intensity 2.50∙10^2 cd; maximum luminous intensity 1.20∙10^3 cd as a single lamp or 6.00∙10^2 cd as a lamp marked "D"; standard light distribution per Figure A3-I; angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum luminous intensity 3∙10^-1 cd.

Direction indicator of category 1b: minimum luminous intensity 4.00∙10^2 cd; maximum luminous intensity 1.20∙10^3 cd as a single lamp or 6.00∙10^2 cd as a lamp marked "D"; standard light distribution per Figure A3-I; angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 with minimum luminous intensity 7∙10^-1 cd.
