Direction indicator lamps: the intensities shall be measured with the light source(s) continuously alight; however, depending on the construction of the lamp (e.g. use of LEDs or need to avoid overheating), measurement in flashing mode is allowed, switching with a frequency of f = 1.5 ± 0.5 Hz with pulse width greater than 0.3 s measured at 95 per cent peak light intensity; in all other cases the voltage required in paragraph 4.8. shall be switched with rise and fall times shorter than 0.01 s and no overshoot.
Direction indicator lamps measured in flashing mode: the reported luminous intensity shall be represented by the maximum intensity.

Direction indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a or 1b may produce the flash by sequential activation of their light sources, provided conditions (a) to (e) of paragraph 5.6.5. are met, verified in flashing mode.
Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): each light source, after its activation, shall remain lit until the end of the ON cycle (verified in flashing mode).

Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the sequence of activation of the light sources shall produce a signal which proceeds in a uniform progressive manner from inboard towards the outboard edge of the light emitting surface (verified in flashing mode).

Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the signal shall be one signal with no interruption and no vertical oscillations (not more than one change of direction along the vertical axis) (verified in flashing mode).

Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the distance between two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the light emitting surface shall not exceed 50 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, instead of the values in paragraph 5.7.2. of UN Regulation No. 48.

Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): interruptions of the signal between distinct parts shall not create any overlap in the vertical axis between the different parts, from inboard towards outboard of the vehicle.
Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the interruptions between distinct parts of the light emitting surface shall not be used for any other lighting or light-signalling functions.
Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the variation shall finish no more than 200 ms after the beginning of the ON cycle (verified in flashing mode).

Sequential direction indicator (categories 1, 1a, 1b): the orthogonal projection of the light emitting surfaces in the direction of the axis of reference shall be circumscribed by a rectangle on a plane normal to the axis of reference with its longer sides parallel to the H-plane, and the ratio of horizontal to vertical sides shall not be less than 1.7.
Direction indicator lamps: the colour of the light emitted shall be amber.
Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under this Regulation, including the requirements of paragraph 5.

Conformity of production: no measured value of a production lamp shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in this Regulation; for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3 the measured values shall correspond to the values in Table 12.

Conformity of production equivalent minimum values (required minimum / 20 per cent equivalent / 30 per cent equivalent): 7∙10^-1 cd / 5∙10^-1 cd / 3∙10^-1 cd; 6∙10^-1 cd / 4∙10^-1 cd / 2∙10^-1 cd; 3∙10^-1 cd / 2∙10^-1 cd / 1∙10^-1 cd; 7∙10^-2 cd / 5∙10^-2 cd / 3∙10^-2 cd; 5∙10^-2 cd / 3∙10^-2 cd / 2∙10^-2 cd.

In case the side corner lamp is a front direction indicator of category 1, 1a or 1b (lamp for the right side of the vehicle), the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally (reduced to 20° / 80° only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15° / 5° for lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm).

In case the side corner lamp is a side direction indicator of category 5, the angles of geometric visibility shall be 5° (A) / 55° (B) horizontally, the horizontal angles applying to direction A, and minimum 15° above / 15° below vertically (reduced to 15° / 5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

In case the side corner lamp is a side marker lamp of category SM1, the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be 45° (A) / 45° (B) horizontally and 10° above / 10° below vertically (reduced to 10° / 5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

In case the side corner lamp is a side marker lamp of category SM2, the minimum angles of geometric visibility shall be 30° (A) / 30° (B) horizontally and 10° above / 10° below vertically (reduced to 10° / 5° for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm).

The luminous intensities of the side signalling lamp in the various directions of measurement shall be at least the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, given as a percentage of the minimum intensities required and mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, the direction H = 0°, V = 0° corresponding to the reference axis passing through the centre of reference; however, where the direction indicator or side marker lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the side signalling lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown (as a percentage) on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

In case the side corner lamp is a direction indicator lamp of category 1, 1a or 1b, its luminous intensities shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, the values giving the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required in Table 8.

In case the side corner lamp is a direction indicator lamp of category 6, its luminous intensities shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-IV (outer side of the vehicle), the direction H = 5°, V = 0° corresponding to the minimum value prescribed in Table 8 and the other values giving the minimum intensities as a percentage of that minimum.
In case the side corner lamp is a side marker lamp of category SM1, its luminous intensities shall meet the light distribution of Figure A3-VII.
In case the side corner lamp is a side marker lamp of category SM2, its luminous intensities shall meet the light distribution of Figure A3-VIII.
From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, production lamps shall not differ from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

When testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. on any production lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
Production lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
In case the lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the side marker and direction indicator lamp (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

In case the lamp has a direction indicator function, the direction indicator shall be operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent) for the luminous intensity measurements after 1 min and after 30 min or photometric stability.

Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the lamp (function) shall, in addition to paragraph 1 of Annex 8, comply at the point in time after switch ON listed in Table A8-1, referenced to the reference coordinate of the lamp (function).
In case the side corner lamp is a side marker lamp, the additional luminous intensity check shall be made at 4 seconds after switch ON, reference coordinate HV.
In case the side corner lamp is a direction indicator of category 1 (1a, 1b), the additional luminous intensity check shall be made at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, reference coordinate HV.
In case the side corner lamp is a direction indicator of category 5 or 6, the additional luminous intensity check shall be made at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, reference coordinate H5, V0.

In case the lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only, it is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.1. of Annex 8 are compliant.

In case the lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. of Annex 8 are compliant.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

The provisions of UN R26 shall not apply to those parts of the bumper module's external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and with all doors, windows and access lids etc. in the closed position, are below the floor line.

The provisions of UN R26 shall not apply to those parts of the bumper module's external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and with all doors, windows and access lids etc. in the closed position, are so located that, in their static condition as well as when in operation, they cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter.

The external surface of the bumper module shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of the bumper module shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the bumper module's external surface (fascia, grille, lamp housings, covers, flaps, sensor covers) shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts which protrude less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the bumper module's external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, the hardness being measured with the component as installed on the vehicle (or by comparable measurements where the Shore A procedure is impossible).

Where an added ornament (e.g. emblem/logo) on the fascia projects more than 10 mm from its support (a base being regarded as belonging to the ornament), it shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at its most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the mounting surface, applied with a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter (or an equivalent method); this does not apply to ornaments on radiator grilles, to which only the general requirements of paragraph 5 apply.

After an added ornament (projecting more than 10 mm, not on the radiator grille) has retracted, become detached or bent over under the 10 daN force, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
The remaining projections of an added ornament after it has retracted, become detached or bent over shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.

The requirements of paragraph 5.4 shall not apply to gaps between fixed or movable elements of the bumper module, including those forming part of air intake or outlet grilles and radiator grilles, provided that the distance between consecutive elements, determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3, does not exceed 40 mm and the grilles and gaps have a functional purpose.
For grille elements and gaps with a distance between consecutive elements of between 40 mm and 25 mm (determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3), the radii of curvature shall be 1 mm or more.

If the distance between two consecutive elements of a grille or gap is equal to or less than 25 mm (determined according to paragraph 4 of Annex 3), the radii of curvature of the external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.

The ends of the bumper shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling; this is considered satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, within the part of that zone situated between and in front of the tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each forming an angle of 15° with the longitudinal plane of symmetry of the vehicle.

If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all cases other than the 5 mm zone (contour line to 20 mm inward between the 15° tangent planes).

The requirement of paragraph 6.5.2 shall not apply to parts on or of the bumper or to bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm (e.g. joint covers), but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The requirement of paragraph 6.5.2 does not apply to the bumper cover (fascia); the provisions of paragraph 5 remain applicable to the bumper cover.
The projection of the fuel tank filler cap / cover (EV charging inlet flap integrated in the fascia) shall not exceed 30 mm.

Where the lower stiffener or other visible bumper component is made of sheet metal with exposed edges on the external surface, sheet-metal edges shall not be permitted unless they are folded back (by approximately 180°, or towards the bodywork so that they cannot be contacted by a sphere of 100 mm diameter) or are fitted with a shield meeting the requirements of this Regulation applicable to it.

Folds in body panels (e.g. the fascia) may have a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm provided that it is not less than one-tenth of the height "H" of the projection, measured in accordance with paragraph 1 of Annex 3.
Where movable air intake or outlet flaps (e.g. active grille shutters) are fitted, they shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 in all positions of use.

The supporting bracket provided by the vehicle manufacturer for the front registration plate shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 5.4 if it is contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.

Where the keyless-entry aerial (or another transmitting/receiving aerial of the module) projects from the external surface, it shall be fitted so that, if its unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the aerial manufacturer, the unattached end is inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.

Aerials of the bumper module shall be so fitted, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.
Shafts of aerials may have radii of curvature of less than 2.5 mm; however, the unattached ends shall be fitted with fixed cappings with radii of curvature not less than 2.5 mm.
The bases of aerials projecting from the external surface shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2 of Annex 3.

Where, due to the absence of a flexible shaft or part, the base of an aerial cannot be identified, the 40 mm base requirement is deemed met if, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN in forward and rearward direction is applied by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient part of the aerial, either (a) the aerial bends towards the support and does not project more than 40 mm, or (b) the aerial breaks off and the remaining part shows no sharp or dangerous part contactable by the 100 mm sphere and does not project more than 40 mm.

The height H of a projection of a fold in the body panels (e.g. the bumper fascia) shall be determined graphically by reference to the circumference of a 165 mm diameter circle internally tangential to the external outline of the external surface at the section checked. H is the maximum distance, measured along a straight line through the centre of the 165 mm circle, between the circumference of that circle and the external contour of the projection.

Where a 100 mm diameter circle cannot contact externally part of the external outline of the external surface at the section considered, the surface outline in that area shall be assumed to be that formed by the circumference of the 100 mm diameter circle between its tangent points with the external outline, for determining the height of fold projections.

The dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a convex external surface (e.g. a lamp, sensor cover, flap or aerial on the fascia) may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the component in its installed condition.

If the dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component.

The dimension of a gap or of the space between elements of the radiator grille shall be determined as the distance between two planes passing through the points of contact of the sphere and perpendicular to the line joining those points of contact.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices (including the side signalling lamp integrated in the front bumper) shall continue to operate correctly.

After each impact test made in accordance with the conditions and procedure specified in Annex 3, the lighting and signalling devices (including the side signalling lamp integrated in the front bumper) shall remain visible.

After each impact test according to Annex 3, the requirement that the vehicle's propulsion, suspension, steering and braking systems remain in adjustment and operate in a normal manner does not apply to sensors, cameras, radar devices, etc. being part of driver assist systems; these may become damaged, disoriented or broken due to an impact carried out according to Annex 3 as long as the basic braking and steering performance are still intact.

Every vehicle bearing an approval mark under this Regulation shall conform to the vehicle type approved, particularly as regards features which influence the behaviour of the parts of the structure and the components affected by impact (e.g. the front protective device).

In both vehicle-loading conditions (unladen weight and laden test weight), the front protective device between the vehicle corners (as defined in paragraph 3.1.5.) shall be intersected by the horizontal plane passing through the impactor reference line at the reference height of 445 mm.
In the low-speed impact tests of Annex 3, the first contact of the impactor with the vehicle shall be by the impact contour on the front protective device.
In the low-speed impact tests of Annex 3, the effective mass of the impactor shall be equal to the mass corresponding to the unladen weight of the vehicle to be tested.

The front protective device shall withstand the longitudinal impact test consisting of two impacts on the front surface of the vehicle: one with the vehicle at unladen weight (paragraph 3.1.3.) and one with the vehicle at laden test weight (paragraph 3.1.4.).

For the longitudinal impacts on the front surface, the location of the first impact is free, but for the second impact the median plane of the impactor shall be at least 300 mm from the first, provided that the extremities of the impactor do not pass outside the zone defined by two planes parallel to the longitudinal median plane passing through the vehicle corners.

For the longitudinal impact test, the impactor is placed with plane A vertical and the reference line horizontal at the reference height of 445 mm, with the vehicle's longitudinal median plane perpendicular to plane A and a point between the vehicle corners touching the impactor.
In the longitudinal impact test, the front of the vehicle is impacted at a speed of 4 km/h +0.25/-0 km/h.

The front protective device shall withstand the corner impact test consisting of an impact at one front corner with the vehicle at unladen weight (paragraph 3.1.3.) and an impact at the other front corner with the vehicle at laden test weight (paragraph 3.1.4.).
For the corner impact test, the impactor is placed with plane A vertical and the reference line horizontal at the reference height of 445 mm.
In the corner impact test, plane A of the impactor shall make an angle of 60 ± 5° with the longitudinal median plane of the vehicle, with a vehicle corner touching the impactor.
In the corner impact test, the point of first contact shall be in the vertical median plane of the impactor within a tolerance of ± 25 mm.
In the corner impact test, the front corner of the vehicle is impacted at a speed of 2.5 km/h +0.1/-0 km/h.
The protective devices and the mountings attaching them to the vehicle structure may be repaired or replaced between the tests.
If the protective devices include self-restoring materials (e.g. energy-absorbing foam), the permitted recovery time between tests shall be as stated by the manufacturer.

If the test has been carried out at an impact speed or with an impact mass exceeding those indicated in paragraphs 2.7.5. and 2.8.4. of Annex 3 and the vehicle has satisfied the prescribed conditions, the test is considered satisfactory.
Other equivalent test methods are permitted provided that the conditions referred to in this Regulation can be observed and their equivalence can be demonstrated.

The side-marker lamp shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
It shall not be possible for the side-marker lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The reference axis of the side-marker lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
The reference axis of the side-marker lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer for the light-signalling device shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, side-marker lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, the estimate being based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface.

In the absence of specific instructions, side-marker lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, side-marker lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, side-marker lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function.
In case of lamps incorporating a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo can be fitted on the front of the vehicle.
In case of lamps incorporating a logo, all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the pair requirements of paragraph 5.5 shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

The side-marker lamp may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with other lamps provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.

Where the side-marker lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with other functions, its photometric and colorimetric requirements shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

Where the lamp is a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(a) whose apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts (e.g. segmented), it shall be installed so that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Where the single lamp is composed of two lamps marked "D" (paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c)), it shall be installed so that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing those projections, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Where the lamp is an interdependent lamp system (paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d)), it shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.; two or more lamps and/or separate apparent surfaces included in the same lamp body and/or having a common outer lens shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

The maximum height of the lamp above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the height clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height of the lamp above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of the lamp as regards width shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane when referred to the overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position clearly meets the requirements, the exact edges need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of the side-marker lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
Amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7. shall be flashing lamps.

The photometric characteristics of the side-marker lamp may vary (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The electrical connections shall be such that the side-marker lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp; this does not apply while (a) side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with position lamps are switched ON as parking lamps, (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators, (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON, or (d) the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
Concealment of the side-marker lamp is prohibited (concealment is permitted only for main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps when not in use).
The colour of the light emitted by the side-marker lamp shall be amber.
The number of side-marker lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
A lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

In case the lamp is approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37 (except when used as non-replaceable light sources as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2.), it shall be fitted so that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

In case the lamp is approved with replaceable light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.
Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to UN Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility of the side-marker lamp to the propagation of light from any part of its apparent surface observed from infinity; however, no account is taken of obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle (e.g. the bumper fascia), proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
An LED module does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

The side-marker lamp shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulation as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48 when installed on a vehicle.
In case of a light-signalling lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

In case the lamp is approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, it shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only; this does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

A device type approved according to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148 is deemed equivalent to one approved according to the latest series when the change indexes related to each individual lamp (function) do not differ, and may then be fitted without any update of the device type approval documents and device markings.

The use of a lamp approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) is allowed exclusively where the statement indicated in paragraph 3.2.8. is present and positive, and the lamp shall bear the marking related to the use of LED substitute light source(s).

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp: direction-indicator lamps are mandatory, and on motor vehicles the assembly of direction-indicator lamp categories shall constitute arrangement "A".

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, the number of direction-indicator lamps shall be according to the arrangement, and the devices shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a front direction-indicator lamp (arrangement A, two front lamps), it may be of category 1, 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of its apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp (if there is one) is at least 40 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a front direction-indicator lamp, it shall be of category 1a or 1b if the distance between the edge of its apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp (if there is one) is greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a front direction-indicator lamp, it shall be of category 1b if the distance between the edge of its apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis and that of the dipped-beam headlamp and/or front fog lamp (if there is one) is less than or equal to 20 mm.

Where an AFS is fitted, the distance to be considered for the choice of the front direction-indicator lamp category is the distance between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a side direction-indicator lamp on an M1 vehicle, two side direction-indicator lamps of at least category 5 shall be fitted; category 5 side direction-indicator lamps may be replaced by category 6 side direction-indicator lamps.

Where lamps combining the functions of front direction-indicator lamps (categories 1, 1a, 1b) and side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) are fitted, two additional side direction-indicator lamps (categories 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall not be less than 600 mm; this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a side direction-indicator lamp of category 5 or 6 on an M1 vehicle, the height of its light-emitting surface above the ground shall not be less than 350 mm, measured from the lowest point.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a side direction-indicator lamp of category 5 or 6, the height of its light-emitting surface above the ground shall not be more than 1,500 mm, measured from the highest point; if the structure of the vehicle does not permit this upper limit to be respected (and optional rear lamps are not installed), it may be increased to 2,300 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a front direction-indicator lamp of category 1, 1a or 1b, its height above the ground, measured in accordance with paragraph 5.8., shall not be less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm; if the structure of the vehicle does not permit the upper limit to be respected (and optional rear lamps are not installed), it may be increased to 2,100 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a side direction-indicator lamp (category 5 or 6), the distance between its light-emitting surface and the transverse plane which marks the forward boundary of the vehicle's overall length shall not exceed 1,800 mm, however for M1 category vehicles this distance shall not exceed 2,500 mm.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp of category 1, 1a, 1b or 5, its geometric visibility shall be ensured over vertical angles of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a side direction-indicator lamp of category 6, its geometric visibility shall be ensured over vertical angles of 30° above and 5° below the horizontal.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, its geometric visibility shall be ensured over the horizontal angles shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.1., the value of 5° given for the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator being an upper limit (d ≤ 2.50 m for M1 category vehicles).

For front direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a and 1b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward horizontal visibility angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Alternatively, at the discretion of the manufacturer for M1 vehicles, the geometric visibility of front direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall be ensured over the horizontal angles shown in the figure of paragraph 6.5.5.2., the value of 5° for the dead angle of visibility to the rear of the side direction-indicator being an upper limit (d ≤ 2.50 m); for direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a and 1b mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where the alternative visibility of paragraph 6.5.5.2. is used for M1 vehicles, front direction-indicator lamps and side-marker lamps shall be visible over vertical angles of 15° above and below the horizontal; where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle may be reduced to 5°.

Where the alternative visibility of paragraph 6.5.5.2. is used, to be considered visible the lamp (front direction-indicator or side-marker lamp, except side direction-indicators of categories 5 and 6) shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm², the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light being excluded.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, its orientation shall be according to the specifications for installation by the manufacturer, if any.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, it shall switch ON independently of the other lamps.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, all direction-indicator lamps on one side of the vehicle shall be switched ON and OFF automatically as defined by applicable UN Regulations and/or by means of one control.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, all direction-indicator lamps on one side of the vehicle shall flash in phase.

On M1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency (in phase) with the direction-indicator lamps.
A direction-indicator lamp capable of being activated in different modes (static or sequential) shall not switch between both modes once activated.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a front direction-indicator lamp of category 1, 1a or 1b, an operating tell-tale is mandatory; it may be visual or auditory or both.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is visual, it shall be a flashing light which, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, is either extinguished, or remains alight without flashing, or shows a marked change of frequency.

If the direction-indicator operating tell-tale is entirely auditory, it shall be clearly audible and shall show a marked change of frequency, at least in the event of the malfunction of any of the direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b.

The direction-indicator operating tell-tale shall be activated by the signal produced according to paragraph 6.2.2. of UN Regulation No. 6, or paragraph 5.6.3. of the 00 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or paragraph 4.6.1.4. of the 01 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148, or another suitable way.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, its light shall be a flashing light flashing 90 ± 30 times per minute.
Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one second by the emission of light.

Where the side signalling lamp is used as a direction-indicator lamp, operation of the light-signal control shall be followed within not more than one and one-half seconds by the first extinction of the light.

In the event of failure, other than short-circuit, of one direction-indicator lamp, the other direction-indicator lamps shall continue to flash, but the frequency in this condition may be different from that prescribed.

On M1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2., the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash in phase, at the same frequency as the direction-indicator lamps, when the hazard warning signal is operated.
Side-marker lamps are mandatory on vehicles whose length exceeds 6 m (except chassis-cabs) and optional on all other vehicles.

On M1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility requirements of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2. and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2.
The SM1 type of side-marker lamp shall be used; however, the SM2 type of side-marker lamp may be used on M1 category vehicles, both where the side-marker lamp is mandatory and where it is optional.
The minimum number of side-marker lamps per side shall be such that the rules for longitudinal positioning are complied with.
Side-marker lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 91, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Side-marker lamp position in height: above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm).

Side-marker lamp position in length: at least one side-marker lamp shall be fitted to the middle third of the vehicle, the foremost side-marker lamp being not further than 3 m from the front; the distance between two adjacent side-marker lamps shall not exceed 3 m (may be increased to 4 m if the structure, design or operational use of the vehicle makes compliance impossible); the distance between the rearmost side-marker lamp and the rear of the vehicle shall not exceed 1 m. However, for vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted within the first third and/or within the last third of the vehicle length, and for M1 vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m but does not exceed 7 m it is sufficient to have one side-marker lamp fitted not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length.

Side-marker lamp geometric visibility, horizontal angle: 45° to the front and to the rear; however, for vehicles on which the installation of side-marker lamps is optional this value can be reduced to 30°.

If the vehicle is equipped with side-marker lamps used to supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front and rear direction-indicator lamps conforming to paragraph 6.5.5.2. and/or position lamps conforming to paragraphs 6.9.5.2. and 6.10.5.2., the horizontal angles of geometric visibility of the side-marker lamps are 45° towards the front and rear ends of the vehicle and 30° towards the centre of the vehicle.

Side-marker lamp geometric visibility, vertical angle: 10° above and below the horizontal; however, where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Side-marker lamp orientation: towards the side.

On M1 category vehicles less than 6 m in length, amber side-marker lamps may be wired to flash, provided that this flashing is in phase and at the same frequency with the direction-indicator lamps at the same side of the vehicle.
Side-marker lamp tell-tale is optional; if it exists, its function shall be carried out by the tell-tale required for the front and rear position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the side-marker lamp is mandatory if required by the component regulation.

When an optional side-marker lamp is grouped or combined with a position lamp that is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with the direction indicator, the electrical connection of the side-marker lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of activation of the direction-indicator lamp.

The position of the side-marker lamp in width, in height and in length, checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of the Regulation, shall be such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to that lamp.

The angles of geometric visibility of the side-marker lamp, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to that lamp; the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of light-signalling devices.

The lamp installed in the bumper shall comply with paragraph 5.10. regarding visibility of red light towards the front, checked in zone 1 of Annex 4, bounded in height by horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground and in width by vertical planes forming an angle of 15° outwards to the front from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane through the foremost point(s) of contact of the planes delimiting the vehicle's overall width.

When switched on via the vehicle electrical system, the side-marker lamp, its electrical connections and any associated tell-tale shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of the Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to that lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of the side-marker lamp, checked by visual inspection of the lamp and its markings, shall fulfil paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and the individual specifications applicable to that lamp.
